thread:
maria: FYI noticed a regression on canary after the kernel-selector tweak — p99 token latency up ~18% for short-seq workloads :thinking:
kevin: any traces/benchmark numbers?
maria: attached numbers from yesterday's load run (mixture of 16/64/512). short sequences used to form batches ~6, now avg batch size ~3 which drives up overheads. KV hit rate also dropped ~4%.
sam: hmm that sounds like microbatch formation issue — maybe the coalesce/jitter changed effective wait window
maria: exactly. I dug into the profiler: more frequent small batches, and KV cache priming seems less effective because microbatches finish earlier before subsequent requests touch same KV entries.
carla: can you paste the perf snippet?
maria: sure — p99s before/after: 
```
before: p50 22ms p90 48ms p99 120ms avg batch size 5.8 kv_hit 86%
after:  p50 24ms p90 56ms p99 142ms avg batch size 3.2 kv_hit 82%
```
kevin: interesting. kernel-selector change probably favored a slightly different kernel path that has lower per-token throughput for small batches but better long-seq perf. need to confirm.
devon: can we try tuning micro_window_ms (micro-batch interval) and coalesce_delay_ms? maybe increase window by 1-2ms to let more arrivals join the batch. also consider adding jitter to avoid synchronized arrivals.
sam: +1. We should also try an age-priority queue where older requests get bumped to form batches sooner — reduces tail latency for waiting short requests.
maria: I ran an A/B locally: bump micro_window_ms from 3ms -> 6ms and coalesce_delay_ms 1ms -> 2ms; p99 dropped back by ~9% but avg latency up slightly. tradeoff looks promising.
carla: did that change KV hit rate?
maria: kv_hit recovered to 84% in the local run. still below baseline but better.
kevin: worth a deeper sweep. propose matrix: micro_window_ms {3,6,9}, coalesce_delay_ms {1,2,4}, jitter_std_ms {0.5,1.5}, queue_policy {fifo, age-priority}. run with seq distribution 16/64/512 weighted 0.6/0.3/0.1 and measure avg batch size, kv_hit, p99.
devon: I'll spin up the sweep script today. command I use: `./tools/bench --model rwd-small --mix 16,64,512 --weights 0.6,0.3,0.1 --duration 30m --collect kpi,json --coalesce-ms 2 --micro-window-ms 6 --jitter-ms 1`
sam: also add a run where kernel-selector is pinned to previous threshold so we can separate kernel vs batching effects.
maria: good call. I'll pin kernel selector on canary for the controlled experiment.
carla: one more thought — KV cache eviction policy may be interacting. if batches are smaller, less opportunity to touch KV for subsequent tokens, so we could adjust kv_ttl or prewarm heuristics for very short sequences.
kevin: noted. add kv_ttl {30s,60s} to the sweep matrix as an orthogonal axis.

deploy-bot: Rollout start: canary/kernel-selector-v2 -> 3 hosts (triggered by kevin) :rocket:

maria: after sweeps let's prioritize setting a safe default: micro_window_ms 6ms, coalesce_delay_ms 2ms, jitter 1ms, queue_policy age-priority, kv_ttl 60s for canary. if p99 still > baseline, revert kernel change.
sam: I'll prepare dashboards: batch-size histogram, kv_hit over time, per-seq-percentile heatmap, kernel-path breakdown.
devon: running first sweep now. ETA ~2h. I'll drop logs in this thread when done.
carla: thanks — please include the raw traces from `perf-trace` and a microtrace showing batch formation timestamps. small text snippet format preferred.
maria: will do. summary action items: (1) sweep matrix runs (devon), (2) pin kernel selector for control (maria), (3) dashboards (sam), (4) kv_ttl probe (carla).
kevin: thanks team. if sweep shows kernel is culprit we'll rollback and iterate on selector heuristics offline. :thumbsup:
